_about: Which catalogue items suit which surface kind (yes / careful / no) and why. Source: round 1, chapter 1 matrix.

fit.why: Dense rows of people and agents; preview without leaving. Phones have no hover, so the app uses tap, and sites don't use it at all.
One bell in the header (ADR 15). The app adds operating-system notifications.
Keyboard power for people who live in it. A model mid-show won't press ⌘K.
Brief confirmations. On a site, only "Message sent".
Activity, sessions and supporters, by day. On a site, only a static "our story".
Comparing records is dashboard work. On a narrow screen a table becomes a list.
Only above about a thousand rows; below that the sortable table is lighter.
The S widget. A site gets one static stats band as social proof ("1,000 sites built").
Is, before, after, between, by day to year: the dashboard's filter. The app needs only "tonight / this week".
One line per step in Agent Base. The Oracle shows steps only when asked.
Agent chat, room chat and the Oracle. A site gets a chatbot later, as one island.
Open detail in place (ADR 5). On a site, only the phone menu, in CSS.
The shell loads once and data streams in (ADR 10). A static page arrives whole.
For us while designing, never for customers.

fit.item: Hero, menu, hours and map, photos, reviews, footer
